#### 1. semantic dementia  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.745)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-264870, Reactome:R-HSA-9619483, Reactome:R-HSA-9833482)

**Proposed mechanism:** MAPT (HGNC:6893) —DISRUPTS→ Tau protein aggregation and neurofibrillary tangle formation (GO:0007414); Tau protein aggregation and neurofibrillary tangle formation (GO:0007414) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodegeneration (HP:0002090); Tau protein aggregation and neurofibrillary tangle formation (GO:0007414) —LEADS_TO→ Cognitive impairment (HP:0001263). Disruption of MAPT function leads to aberrant tau protein aggregation and neurofibrillary tangle formation, ultimately causing neurodegeneration (progressive supranuclear palsy) and cognitive impairment (semantic dementia).

**How to falsify it:** The absence of MAPT mutations in individuals diagnosed with either progressive supranuclear palsy or semantic dementia, or the identification of completely distinct molecular pathways driving these conditions, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs1042539)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MAPT in these neurodegenerative diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at modulating tau pathology, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.
